tldr: Headlines across all 13 buckets treat Karim Khan's removal as a misconduct-driven dismissal, splitting between outlets that foreground the sexual allegations in the title and those that foreground the member-state vote mechanism; only two Asian outlets (Malay Mail, The Hindu) inject geopolitical framing — the Netanyahu warrant and U.S. sanctions — context absent from every other bucket's headline.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only headline to connect Khan's removal explicitly to the Netanyahu arrest warrant — framing the dismissal through a Middle East politics lens that no other outlet invokes at the title level.

The only headline to mention U.S. sanctions as a constraining factor, introducing the geopolitical dimension (Khan barred from attending his own hearing) that the body text of other outlets buries well below the fold.

The only outlet to publish a profile/explainer headline ('Who is Karim Khan, the barrister at the centre of the ICC's internal crisis?') instead of a news-event headline, foregrounding institutional identity over the removal verdict.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, this story is split between a misconduct-dismissal frame (Western wire and anglophone outlets) and an institutional-vote frame (Asian and Global South outlets), with only two headlines surfacing the geopolitical stakes — U.S. sanctions and the Netanyahu warrant — that body coverage develops at length.
